label: early original-phase steps after a leading n (n at position 0, or at position 1)
explanation: Fires during the original phase at steps 2-4 when the sequence begins with the letter n (first_tok=n has 18x lift and holds 88% of activation mass). It is strongest at step 3 (about 1.0 of max), weaker at step 4 (~0.7) and step 2 (~0.1-0.16); a second n at position 1 does not change this. A weaker version fires at steps 3-4 when n is the second original token (orig(1)=n), typically at 0.2-0.5 of max. What comes after the n barely matters (prev_tok d/p add a small boost). Mostly silent at steps 0-1, at steps >=5, on the <DEL> step, and in the copy phase (under 2% of mass). The remaining misses are very weak activations (under 0.1 of max) on sequences with no early n. The feature behaves like a short-lived memory of an n near the start, decaying about 2-4 steps later.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says step 2 fires at only about 0.1-0.16 of max, but on test the clause orig(0)=n & t=2 has precision 1.0, count recall 0.207 and mass recall 0.277. The t=3 clause has count recall 0.202 and mass recall 0.428. So the mean activation at step 2 is about 0.65 of step 3, close to step 4 (count recall 0.162, mass recall 0.162). The profile agrees: t=2 holds 29% of mass, t=3 holds 51% and t=4 holds 18%. Step 3 is the peak, but step 2 is not weak.

The orig(1)=n branch is weak and only half reliable. On test it has precision 0.60 and mass recall 0.13 (t=3: precision 0.74; t=4: precision 0.43). Most of the predicate's 12.7k false positives are sequences like 'p n w o', 'd n 1 k', 's n c o' that never fire. 'Usually at 0.2-0.5 of max' overstates how often it fires.

'Under 2% of mass combined' for off-window steps is slightly low. t=5 holds 1.0%, <DEL> 1.0% and copy 0.5%, so about 2-2.5%. Some of the <DEL> mass is a structured miss: for short L, a <DEL> landing at t=3-4 after a leading n fires (e.g. 'n v a <DEL>:0.32'). Adding the delimiter phase raises recall but lowers precision (test F1 0.796, worse than 0.806).
Another small structured miss: sequences starting 'n n' keep firing at t=5 (0.3-0.5). Extending the window to t=5 hurts F1 overall (0.69-0.74).
The other misses are scattered very weak t=2 activations without an early n (precision 0.025, mass 1.3%), which is noise as the explanation says. This is why bottom-quartile coverage is only 0.26.
The label and predicate themselves hold up: the test scores reproduce (precision 0.831, recall 0.782, F1 0.806, mass recall 0.962), and none of the variants I tried beat them.
